counterfactual_missing_items: Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species grew in blood cultures
decisive_items: After 10 days of fever with an absolute neutrophil count of 20/μL
High-resolution chest CT showed nonspecific nodules under 1 cm
MRI of the right shoulder demonstrated a focal cystic necrotic lesion between the teres minor and teres major muscles
response.rationale: R6 best integrates prolonged neutropenic fever, pulmonary nodules, and a necrotic muscle lesion as disseminated invasive fungal infection, whereas R1 only names the MRI soft-tissue lesion without a microbial cause and does not explain the pulmonary nodules. Negative galactomannan is a counterweight but does not exclude mold infection.

rejected.why: Coagulase-negative staphylococcal bacteremia is a common contaminant/catheter infection and does not explain the persistent fever or necrotic muscle lesion after appropriate antibiotics.
Febrile neutropenia is the predisposing syndrome, not the tissue diagnosis, and does not account for the focal cystic necrotic lesion.
Herpes zoster is suggested by radiating pain but is contradicted by absent vesicles and by the MRI necrotic lesion.
Acute lymphoblastic leukemia is the established underlying disease and provides context, but it is not the new focal diagnostic question.
